premise: When my mother died, her will left me her $200,000 collection of vintage Barbie dolls, but my stepsister—the executor—forged a $1 sale note and sold the entire collection to a private collector for $240,000. I found a dated voicemail from Mom assigning me the dolls, voided the sale in probate, and now run “Dollhouse of Deceit” — my stepsister dresses and dusts the display dolls in a smock that reads “Plastic Promises,” and each doll’s packaging features a QR code to her fraud conviction.
